title: Invert sugar: what it means for your plan
standfirst: Which of our plan rules this ingredient turns on, and what that does not tell you.

spans.text: Invert sugar: a syrup of glucose and fructose made by splitting sucrose, valued for sweetness and keeping baked goods moist.
Why it is in your food
Manufacturers use invert sugar as a sweetener/sugar and it is of plant origin.
Our rules read invert sugar as a refined syrup.

Our scorer looks for invert sugar when Autoimmune Protocol (AIP), Diabetes, Gout or Fatty liver (NAFLD) is on for you. If those plans are off, your score does not change. This is how the app reads a label. It is not a claim about health.
Labels do not all use the same word for this. Below is every spelling we watch for. Some come from other languages, because a pack made for another country prints its own.
One word on a label can cover more than one thing. A plan may also turn on how much is in the food, which this page cannot see. Read the pack when it matters.
